Hi Olivia — thanks for the annex and clear ask. We can provide both a NIST mapping and an EU AI Act posture summary plus a pragmatic sampling/eval plan. High level commitments below; we will follow with a consolidated packet that includes evidence pointers and an editable mapping CSV.

High-level answers:
- NIST AI RMF: We map our controls to the Core Functions (Govern, Map, Measure, Manage, Govern) with traceability to artifacts (model card, eval reports, deployment configs, access logs). We can supply a versioned mapping PDF and the underlying CSV.
- EU AI Act: Based on the deployment pattern you described (PII processing + clinical triage inference), we anticipate classification as "high-risk" under Annex III. Redwood offers additional contractual safeguards (data residency, private deployment options, KMS integrations) and technical mitigations (explainability hooks, expanded logging, stricter QA gating) to address obligations.
- Eval & regression approach: We suggest a two-tier cadence — continuous smoke checks on production traffic and scheduled regression sampling monthly (stratified by model version, input source, and latency buckets). We will provide a sampling plan and automated regression harness details.

Deliverables & timeline:
- Draft NIST mapping (PDF + CSV) — 5 business days
- EU AI Act posture summary + controls matrix (XLSX) — 5 business days
- Eval sampling plan (CSV) + summary — 4 business days

I'll pull Marissa and Jonas into the thread; they will help assemble evidence and the sampling harness snippets.

Regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

Hi Olivia — attaching the materials we discussed. Summary and key points below. Please let me know if you want a redline-friendly CSV for the mapping or a short walkthrough call.

Summary highlights:
- NIST mapping: attached PDF (redwood_nist_mapping_v2.pdf) maps our policies, operational controls, and artifacts to NIST Core outcomes. Each mapping row references example evidence (model card, eval report, deployment manifest, access logs). We note which artifacts are generated by default in Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployments.
- EU AI Act posture: attached XLSX (eu_act_risk_summary.xlsx) includes our suggested obligations matrix and optional contractual clauses we can accept for high-risk deployments (data residency, restricted subprocessors, expanded logging retention). We call out specific technical mitigations (explainability endpoints, strict input validation, deterministic tracing).
- Eval & regression approach: attached CSV (eval_sampling_plan.csv) with a stratified monthly sampling plan and a recommended regression cadence:
  * Continuous: smoke tests on every model rollout (latency, token-sanity, error rates)
  * Monthly: stratified regression sample of 1% traffic OR minimum 2,500 samples (whichever larger), sampled across model versions and input cohorts (clinical triage, admin text, long-form notes)
  * Triggered: automatic gating on model-promoted regressions or metric drop (>=5% accuracy decline on core prompts)

Evidence availability & timelines: most mapping artifacts can be exported immediately; private deployment audit logs are available on an agreed retention schedule. We can provide the full packet (attachments + editable CSV/XLSX) under the SHARE link below within 24 hours.

Attachments: redwood_nist_mapping_v2.pdf, eu_act_risk_summary.xlsx, eval_sampling_plan.csv
Related link: https://redwood-inference.sharepoint.com/teams/argenta/RFP/ARG-2026-1072
